title: Risk and albuminuria screening
guide: RISK: 50-60% of diabetic patients, ↑ with age; T1 DM screen 5 yearly, T2 DM at diagnosis. Screening: check for albuminuria every 3-6 months — 24-hr urine protein (superior, but cumbersome) or early morning albumin:creatinine (ACR). Levels: <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria (endothelial injury, ↑ thrombosis risk); >300 albuminuria.

title: Hyperfiltration pathogenesis and the SGLT2i mechanism
guide: Afferent vasodilation + efferent vasoconstriction → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension. Net ↓ afferent resistance: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, ANF, angiotensin (↓); net ↑ efferent resistance: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA). Panels: A normal (appropriate tone, normal TGF/GFR); B early DN (afferent vasodilation + ↑ Na/glucose reabsorption → ↓ Na delivery to macula densa → impaired TGF); C SGLT2i (proximal Na reabsorption ↓ → ↑ Na to macula densa → afferent constriction → GFR normalized; glucosuria). SGLT2i: 1st line for hyperfiltration injury.

title: Mogensen staging (T1 DM model)
guide: Mogensen: on the model of T1 DM; not very accurate for T2 DM; stage V = ESRD. Table: I hyperfiltration (GFR ↑, BP =/↑); II silent + microalbuminuria (GFR ↓/↑, BP ↑ — 24-hr ambulatory monitoring: absence of nocturnal dipping, wide pulse pressure); III macroalbuminuria (GFR =/↓, BP ↑↑); IV renal impairment (GFR ↓, BP ↑↑↑).

title: Traver histology, nodular diseases and DN criteria
guide: Traver et al: histological; characteristic pattern nodular glomerulosclerosis. I GBM thickening (earliest); II mesangial expansion (m/c 90%; afferent & efferent hyalinosis); III nodular sclerosis — KW lesions (Kimmelstiel wilson), only 50% pts, most specific; IV advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis. Nodular kidney diseases: diabetes (KW nodules), MPGN, lichen deposition diseases, amyloidosis, smokers. Diabetic nephropathy = albuminuric DKD; criteria (all of): proteinuria (albuminuria) nephrotic range without syndrome; no micro/macro hematuria.

title: DN criteria continued, non-albuminuric DKD and NDRD red flags
guide: Criteria continue: hypertension; edema extra > intravascular d/t Na⁺, glucose transporters; retinopathy concordance T1 100%, T2 65%; if any absent → biopsy. Non-albuminuric DKD: tubulointerstitial & vascular damage. Non-diabetic RPD: nephrotic syndrome; renal dysfunction onset <10y of DM (T1 > T2); absent nephropathy (T1 > T2); mx biopsy; hematuria/RBC casts; extra-renal vasculitis, myeloma; RPRF. Hypertension in DKD diagram: exogenous + genetic → obesity ↔ T2DM → insulin resistance/hyperleptinemia, hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia → sympathetic activation, micro/macrovasculopathy → angiotensin II → hypertension.

title: Management: glucose target, DM drug table, proteinuria control
guide: Target glucose >7 mg/dl as printed (to avoid hypoglycemia). DM control & weight loss: lifestyle; DOC metformin if GFR >30 ml/min. Macrovascular (CKD/ASCVD): DOC SGLT2i — canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin; initiated GFR >30. Table: metformin neutral/neutral-potential benefit/high/low/neutral; SGLT2i benefit/benefit/benefit/intermediate/low/loss; GLP-1 benefit/benefit/potential benefit/high/low/loss; DPP-4 neutral/neutral/potential risk (saxagliptin)/intermediate/low/neutral; insulin neutral/neutral/neutral/highest/high/gain; sulfonylureas neutral/high/high/gain; TZD neutral/potential benefit (pioglitazone)/increased risk/high/low/gain; α-glucosidase inhibitors neutral/neutral/neutral/intermediate/low/neutral. Proteinuria: 1st line SGLT2i + ACEi; 2nd line finerenone (non-steroidal MRA) — monitor s. K⁺ (hyperkalemia risk).

title: Other DM drugs in CKD: preferred agents and eGFRD-safe list
sec: Other DM drugs in CKD · p818
guide: GLP-1 RA: most preferred liraglutide; oral semaglutide; no dose adjustment. DPP-4: most preferred linagliptin (no dose adjustment); others require adjustment. Sulfonylureas: not preferred; renal safe glipizide, gliclazide. Drugs safe in eGFRD: insulin; glipizide, gliclazide; imeglimin (CKD) = oxidative phosphorylation blocker.
